newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds rise on US jobs data, more gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds rise on US jobs data, more gains seen.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose on Thursday after benign U.S. unemployment data and a dealer expected further gains on Friday.
"The American numbers were fantastically positive and made the whole market rise. We now feel sure that interest rates will not raised in the United States at any time soon," he said.
The tone-setting seven percent 2007 government bond, due officially to become the benchmark on September 1, closed up 0.31 point, at 105.88 yielding 6.20 percent.
Its spread to the bund was unchanged at 60 basis points.
Turnover in the 2007 was 2.8 billion crowns.
The crown was virtually unchanged at 3.8074 to the mark.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 rose 0.40 point to 91.70.
"The American numbers caused many foreign buyers to go after Danish bonds and at the same Danish institutional investors have been shopping," the dealer said.
He added that medium-term maturities, up to 10 years, were especially popular but there had been some selling of 30-year paper. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
